sections.h2: Who handles property tax for a McCreary County parcel?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work. One, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), sets values; the other, the Sheriff, receives payment. McCreary County adds a twist: with no incorporated city anywhere inside its lines, there is no city hall tax office and no city levy. County government is the one local government covering every resident.

Mail for the PVA goes to PO Box 609, Whitley City, KY 42653, by phone at (606) 376-2514, and faxes go to (606) 376-4152. Dial (606) 376-2322 for the Sheriff and (606) 376-2411 for the County Clerk, who files deeds and later inherits any unpaid bill. The fiscal court works from 1 North Main Street in Whitley City and hears public business each second Thursday evening, starting at six.

sections.h2: When do penalties begin on a McCreary County bill?
sections.html:
The state schedule, KRS 134.015, measures value on January 1 and wants the bill settled before the year ends. The Sheriff keeps the window open through April 15, with higher costs at each step:

  • Pay it all by November 1 and 2 percent disappears.
  • November 2 to New Year's Eve: the printed total.
  • January: 5 percent more.
  • After that: 10 percent more.

The 2026 discount cutoff is history, which leaves the printed figure until December 31 and a penalty after it. The County Clerk inherits anything unpaid when April 15 ends. Two mailed warnings from the county attorney follow, then a sale scheduled three to four and a half months after the transfer. Whoever buys the certificate may add charges, so settle with the Sheriff first.

sections.h2: What does a McCreary County house cost in tax?
sections.html:
Very little, by Kentucky standards, because values here are low. A typical owned home here is worth $85,300 according to Census, compared with $188,100 in McCracken County. At the state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents on every $100, Frankfort's share is about $90.42. The county, school board and special districts levy more, and the PVA can total them for one address.

With zero permits in 2025, the roll gains little from new building, and the market is existing houses. The Census Bureau's 2020 count, which Wikipedia reports, listed 6,892 housing units with one in eight empty, and 17.9 percent of residents now are 65 or older.

sections.h2: Does McCreary County offer a homestead deduction?
sections.html:
Yes, because the program is statewide. A homeowner who is 65 or older, or classed as totally disabled, has $49,100 removed from assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 years, ahead of the rates.

The subtraction bites hard in this county. At the $85,300 median, only $36,200 stays taxable, and the state's piece drops from about $90.42 to about $38.37. The application is made in person at the Whitley City PVA office, with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport as proof of age. Claims based on disability rest on a government or retirement-plan finding of total disability and are renewed every year. Service-connected veterans, and anyone already judged totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems, are spared the renewal.

sections.h2: What can a McCreary County owner do about an assessment?
sections.html:
Ask for a meeting with the PVA or a deputy before anything else, because Kentucky refuses appeals from owners who skipped it. Staff must explain how the number was produced. After that:

  • Review the roll during the 13 days after the first Monday in May.
  • Hand the appeal to the County Clerk no later than the first working day after the roll closes.
  • Attach evidence on land and structures: insurance records, build costs, comparable sales and photographs. A survey helps with rural tracts. Unsupported appeals fail.
  • Show up when the board of local property owners meets, about a month after the roll closes. It hears evidence only with both sides present.

Missing the hearing forfeits the next stage, the Kentucky Claims Commission. If bills have already printed and the board's value exceeds your claim, a supplemental bill makes up the difference.

sections.h2: What if McCreary County taxes are still owed when the house sells?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax stays attached to the house. The statute treats it as the owner's personal debt from January 1, and a KRS 134.420 lien can last 11 years whichever name is on the deed. Once the bill reaches the Clerk, monthly interest of 1 percent begins, with commissions for the Clerk and county attorney and a recording fee on top.

A title company will want a payoff figure before it releases funds. The Sheriff supplies it up to April 15, and the Clerk after that.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in McCreary County?
sections.html:
The newest of Kentucky's 120 counties, McCreary was cut from Pulaski, Wayne and Whitley in 1912. Its 431 square miles lie along the western rim of the Cumberland Plateau, and no part of it lies inside an incorporated city, which no other Kentucky county can say. Whitley City is the seat, with Pine Knot and Stearns as the other census-designated places. Federal land dominates the map: the Daniel Boone National Forest holds roughly 43 percent and the Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area roughly 18 percent, so private acreage is a limited share.

Early livelihoods came from timber, coal and the Cincinnati Southern Railway, which arrived in 1880 and fed the Stearns company town. Cumberland Falls, a state park since 1930, and the Big South Fork Scenic Railway draw visitors now. Students all attend the McCreary County School District, and McCreary Central High School is its main campus. Clocks follow Eastern time, and the 2025 population of 17,124 is 1.4 percent above 2020.

The average worker needs 32.3 minutes to reach a job, and 80.1 percent of households subscribe to broadband. Pulaski, Laurel, Whitley and Wayne counties border it, along with two Tennessee counties. For an heir to a house here, or an owner behind on tax, a cash sale as-is skips repair bills. The sale price still has to clear the tax payoff, so get that number early.

Population peaked at 18,306 in 2010, and the 2020 count of 16,888 was a 7.7 percent drop. Census business data list 157 employer establishments with 1,522 jobs in 2023, a 4.3 percent decline from the year before, and retail sales near $110 million in 2022. Census lists 8.5 percent of adults with a four-year degree and 18.8 percent of residents under 65 with a disability. Pricing near the county's low median value matters in a market like that, and the Census median gross rent of $577 shows what nearby rental demand will support.

faqs.q: Is there a city property tax in McCreary County?
faqs.a: No. McCreary is the only Kentucky county without an incorporated city, so no city levy exists. School and district levies still appear on the bill.

faqs.q: Whom do I pay for McCreary County property tax?
faqs.a: Hand it to the Sheriff, at (606) 376-2322, any time through April 15. The PVA at (606) 376-2514 sets values and receives exemption papers, never money.

faqs.q: What does the state collect on an $85,300 McCreary County house?
faqs.a: Roughly $90.42, at the state's 2025 rate of 10.6 cents per $100. Local rates add to that.

faqs.q: Can a 65-year-old in McCreary County shrink the taxable value?
faqs.a: Yes. Bring proof of age to the PVA office and $49,100 comes off assessed value for 2025 and 2026 under the homestead deduction.

faqs.q: What if my McCreary County bill moves to the County Clerk?
faqs.a: A lien is recorded and interest runs at 1 percent monthly. The certificate may be sold to an investor three to four and a half months after the move.
